title: Module Header and Axiom Accounting
content: Module docstring: the A_n analogue of Erdős #1162. Explains the free-upper / deep-lower decomposition and the self-contained two-axiom accounting.
mathContext: Writing $g(n)=|\{H\le A_n\}|$, the entry proves $g(n)\le f(n)$ unconditionally, inherits the upper half of the asymptotic from the parent Roney–Dougal–Tracey $S_n$ result, and adds one new axiom (the $A_n$ lower bound) to obtain $\log g(n)=(\tfrac1{16}+o(1))n^2$.

title: numSubgroups: the S_n baseline
content: f(n) = Nat.card (Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) and the re-declared Roney–Dougal–Tracey axiom, kept self-contained so the file does not depend on the (import-drifted) parent.
mathContext: $f(n)=|\{H\le S_n\}|$ with the parent asymptotic $\log f(n)/n^2\to 1/16$ axiomatized as roney_dougal_tracey [RoTr25].

title: numSubgroupsAn: counting subgroups of A_n
content: g(n) = Nat.card (Subgroup (alternatingGroup (Fin n))), realizing A_n as a Subgroup of Equiv.Perm (Fin n) viewed as a group; numSubgroupsAn_pos records g(n) ≥ 1 via the trivial subgroup.
mathContext: $g(n)=|\{H\le A_n\}|$. Since $A_n$ is finite, $\mathrm{Subgroup}(A_n)$ is a finite type and $\mathrm{Nat.card}$ is well-defined and positive (the trivial subgroup $\bot$ always exists).
prerequisites: The alternating group as a subgroup of S_n

title: numSubgroupsAn_le: g(n) ≤ f(n) UNCONDITIONALLY
content: The heart of the free upper half: A_n ↪ S_n is an injective hom, so Subgroup.map along its subtype is injective on the subgroup lattice, and Nat.card is monotone under injections into the finite type Subgroup(S_n). No axiom used.
mathContext: The inclusion $\iota:A_n\hookrightarrow S_n$ is injective, hence $H\mapsto \iota_*(H)=H.\mathrm{map}\,\iota$ is injective on subgroup lattices (Subgroup.map_injective). As $\mathrm{Subgroup}(S_n)$ is finite, $\mathrm{Nat.card}$ monotonicity gives $g(n)\le f(n)$.

title: log/ratio transfer to the normalized asymptotic
content: Monotonicity of log (log_numSubgroupsAn_le) and division by n² (An_ratio_le) push the count bound into the n²-normalized log ratio, so log g(n)/n² ≤ log f(n)/n² for all n.
mathContext: From $g(n)\le f(n)$ and $g(n)\ge 1$, monotonicity of $\log$ gives $\log g(n)\le\log f(n)$; dividing by $n^2\ge 0$ preserves the inequality (both sides are $0$ at $n=0$).

title: An_ratio_eventually_lt: the upper half is FREE
content: Using ONLY the parent RDT asymptotic, the A_n ratio is eventually below 1/16 + ε for every ε > 0 — i.e. limsup log g(n)/n² ≤ 1/16 with no new axiom.
mathContext: $\limsup_n \log g(n)/n^2 \le 1/16$: for each $\varepsilon>0$, eventually $\log f(n)/n^2 < 1/16+\varepsilon$ (from RDT), and $\log g(n)/n^2 \le \log f(n)/n^2$ gives the same bound for $g$.

title: An_lower_bound: the single new axiom
content: The only genuinely new input: the matching A_n lower bound. Justified because A_n retains the dominant elementary abelian 2-subgroups (even-weight products of disjoint transpositions, rank ⌊n/2⌋−1 on ≈ n/4 support), so the constant stays 1/16 = (1/4)².
mathContext: $\liminf_n \log g(n)/n^2 \ge 1/16$. The dominant subgroup contribution comes from elementary abelian $2$-groups on $\approx n/4$ points, and $A_n$ contains these, so the leading constant is unchanged from $S_n$.

title: alternating_asymptotic and pyber_alternating
content: Combining the free upper half with the one lower-bound axiom yields the full A_n asymptotic log g(n) = (1/16 + o(1))n², and the Pyber-analog c₁n² ≤ log g(n) ≤ c₂n² for large n follows (proved, no extra axiom).
mathContext: $\log g(n)/n^2 \to 1/16$ (alternating_asymptotic) and hence $\tfrac1{32}n^2 \le \log g(n) \le \tfrac3{32}n^2$ for large $n$ (pyber_alternating), exactly mirroring how Pyber's theorem follows from RDT for $S_n$.
